refuted.point: Proposal defines explicit PageHead L3 metrics for 4 of 5 modules (Commons, Network, Workbench, Records) — each with exactly 3 metrics in identical teal/amber/coral structure
refuted.why: Charter §8 anti-slop: 'Decorative metrics with no operational meaning' prohibited. User ruling #3: 'Do not force every page into an identical four-metric header. Establish one hierarchy and let the information determine how much of it appears. Consistency must not become ceremony.' The proposal forces symmetry — 3 metrics per module, always teal/amber/coral — where Intelligence correctly gets zero L3. This is ritualization, not hierarchy.
refuted.fix: Remove prescribed L3 metric slots from the direction. Define L1/L2/L3 slots in PageHead component but let each module's actual work surface determine if/which metrics appear. Keep the teal-first left-border convention but make metric count and semantics module-specific and data-driven.

refuted.point: Proposal keeps 'Surveyor grid (24px) as subtle background on work surfaces' as a KEEP item in Signature Devices
refuted.why: Repo-facts §Absences: 'No surveyor grid... in src' (grep-verified). Charter §8 lists it as a signature device but the repo has no implementation. The proposal treats it as already-decided KEEP without verifying it exists or has been approved for v2. This risks agent taste overriding repo reality.
refuted.fix: Move Surveyor grid from KEEP to PROPOSED in Signature Devices. Require a separate design decision with implementation verification before inclusion.

refuted.point: Proposal includes 'Fork glyph (└─) as identity device only (not navigation)' in KEEP
refuted.why: Repo-facts §Absences: 'No fork glyph... in src' (grep-verified). Same issue — treated as already-decided KEEP without repo verification. User ruling #1: 'The fork glyph may remain as an identity element' — this is a user ruling (authority level 1), so it CAN stay, but the proposal presents it as if it already exists in the codebase.
refuted.fix: Clarify: fork glyph is APPROVED by user ruling (not repo-verified). Keep in KEEP but annotate as 'user-ruled, not yet implemented'.

refuted.point: Proposal cuts 'All-caps micro-labels / eyebrows' but keeps 'Uppercase mono allowed ONLY for informational pane headers (rail tooltips, sidebar section labels, dock tab labels, statusbar)' in TYPE decision
refuted.why: Charter §8 anti-slop: 'Decorative all-caps eyebrows' prohibited. The TYPE decision creates a loophole — 'informational pane headers' — that could reintroduce the very micro-labels/eyebrows the CUT list removes. Rail tooltips, sidebar labels, dock tabs, statusbar are exactly where 'eyebrows' appeared in v1 studies.
refuted.fix: Remove the uppercase mono allowance for pane headers. Use mono 8px with letter-spacing for ALL informational text. Reserve uppercase mono for true instrument readouts only (IDs, timestamps, state codes) — never for labels.

refuted.point: Proposal defines contrast facts table with 'dim #5C6B5E 3.4:1 (decorative-only, never primary text)'
refuted.why: WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18pt+). 3.4:1 fails AA for normal text and only passes for large text. Charter §8 provides 'exact palette with contrast requirements' but the proposal's dim token at 3.4:1 is below AA for body text. The 'decorative-only' qualifier is correct but the table presents it as a verified fact without the WCAG nuance.
refuted.fix: Annotate dim token: '3.4:1 — passes WCAG AA only for large text (≥18pt/14pt bold). Use only for decorative/secondary large text. Never for body copy.'

refuted.point: Proposal build_order step 1: 'Define dark-signature token primitives in styles.css (:root = dark default, [data-skin='light'] = light variant) with semantic alias table (canonical/active/risk/gap replacing ok/warn/info/danger)'
refuted.why: Repo-facts §Design tokens: 'Current system is light-first "field atlas"... a .dark class overrides to terminal look.' The proposal inverts this correctly per charter §8 'Dark is the signature system. Light is a variant.' BUT repo-facts notes 'Auth-page styles (~lines 239–595) sit in styles.css' and AGENTS.md says 'Put shared visual tokens and auth-page styles in src/styles.css; reuse controls from src/components/'. The token flip must not break Auth/Landing. Risk noted but not fully mitigated in build_order.
refuted.fix: Add explicit build_order step before 1: 'Audit all token usages in src/ (grep for var(--)) to map light-first dependencies. Create semantic alias mapping table. Verify Auth/Landing pages use only semantic tokens (not skin-specific values) before flip.'
